repair_of.failure: 170 full rows measured 39.6 MB decoded, above the 32 MiB entry cap; no cache retained. Every request fetched full rows and repeated 885–950 ms sizing. Previous evidence fixture retained 19.7 MB and did not reproduce that failure.

implementation.sql: Only list_for_directory selects _DIRECTORY_COLUMNS: fleet projection plus three risk-context references, and no updated_at/lease/retry columns. authoritative_readback objects become the same empty object marker as existing fleet SQL. Result keeps paper_running/status only. JSON object/null behavior remains the existing fleet contract.
implementation.cache: Existing transactional revision trigger and REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot retained; one revision SELECT every call, one row SELECT on changed/missing stamp, detached response copies and fail closed on SQL errors. No TTL. Size graph walk happens once for a loaded scope/stamp; hits do not size. Oversized scopes retain only (stamp,None,measured_size) in a bounded LRU slot, so repeated bypasses at the same stamp reload rows but reuse size. LRU eviction discards the scope and its size metadata. Warning names stamp, tenant, size_bytes and cap_bytes once per observed oversized global revision per store.
implementation.full_reads: get/get_by_persona/list_by_tenant/list_all, reserve/acquire/checkpoint/release, coordinator, readback and create response keep full-row SQL. Legacy fleet methods are unchanged. No agent-provisioning function edited.
implementation.budget: Per store <=8 tenant/all-tenant slots, <=32 MiB each and <=64 MiB retained input graphs in total. Negative slots retain no row objects and share the 8-slot limit. One integer suppresses repeated bypass warnings; no new table, recurring job or file. Fixed LRU bookkeeping/lock overhead and transient decoded rows/response copies are separate from retained-graph budget.

fixture.construction: Synthetic, private-data-free ledger. Each key occurs the recorded number of times. Aggregate JSON text targets recorded key bytes x2.12 (matching ~17.6 MB aggregate wire text); each receipt has 75 distinct nested sequence/digest mappings plus random/compressible owner receipt text. This recreates decoded Python graph overhead as well as wire bytes, rather than one large string; each preserved request carries 4,400 description bytes and 600 mandate bytes so the slim entry also matches the recorded ~1.25 MB. No hosted raw ledger exported. PostgreSQL TOAST storage depends on actual receipt content; exact local storage/text/decoded sizes are measured below, not asserted identical to hosted.
fixture.risk_and_conflicts: One succeeded row carries all three risk keys; the other three each carry one separately. Include error.owner_decision_request fallback, compensation, readback-start and cleanup metadata. One provisioning row raises real ProvisioningConflict against Agora Servant owner name; retired persona-c6ef44745087d11cc138 has no Persona owner. Full snapshots and both real HTTP payloads compare exactly cold and warm.
fixture.deterministic_guard: Decoded full-row graph must be 39–42 MB (above 32 MiB), slim entry must be 1.2–1.5 MB and retain, eight key counts/text budgets must match. Timings and RSS are observations, never test thresholds.
fixture.compression_limit: Local stored references 8,044,909 B vs task-author 5.3 MB hosted: synthetic random nested receipts compress differently. Measured references text 17,588,147 B and decoded full/slim graphs 39.53/1.27 MB match the failure/retention scales; no claim that TOAST compressed bytes or contents are identical.
